deserialization-security.description: JSON/XML deserialization security, validation bypass detection, and gadget chain prevention

evals.name: Mixed legitimate and empty key usage in nested structures
assertions: The response identifies that the empty key in the nested object represents a potential security concern even though the validation passes
The response explains that post-deserialization validation cannot detect the empty key's presence because it examines the resulting object state rather than the JSON structure that was parsed
The response recommends intercepting and validating the raw JSON before Jackson deserialization occurs

evals.name: Duplicate keys used to bypass upstream and application-level validation
evals.prompt:
We have a multi-layer validation setup for our JSON API. Our WAF validates incoming JSON and checks that the 'role' field is one of ['user', 'guest']. Then our application deserializes with Jackson and validates again that role is either 'user' or 'guest' before granting access. Someone submitted:

{
  "username": "attacker",
  "role": "user",
  "role": "admin"
}

The WAF passed it (it saw role='user' first), and when I inspect the deserialized object in our application, obj.getRole() returns 'admin'. Our validation rejected it. But I'm worried—did anything dangerous already happen during deserialization even though we rejected the final object?
assertions: The response confirms that Jackson's 'last value wins' behavior for duplicate keys means the deserialized object has role='admin' despite the WAF seeing role='user'

The response explains that while application-level validation correctly rejected the object, any side effects triggered during Jackson's deserialization process (such as setter methods being called twice or intermediate state changes) would have already occurred
The response recommends raw JSON validation before deserialization to detect and reject duplicate keys, preventing deserialization from occurring with malformed input

evals.name: Polymorphic deserialization with seemingly safe but exploitable subtype
evals.prompt:
Our Java service deserializes JSON into a Command interface with @JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.CLASS). We whitelist known implementations: ReadCommand, WriteCommand, DeleteCommand. During a security review, someone pointed out that one of our dependencies includes a class 'org.example.LoggingCommand' that implements Command and has a setter that writes to arbitrary files when called. This class is on our classpath but NOT in our whitelist of expected types. If an attacker sends:

{
  "@class": "org.example.LoggingCommand",
  "logFile": "/etc/passwd",
  "message": "pwned"
}

Jackson will deserialize it. Our post-deserialization validation checks 'instanceof ReadCommand || instanceof WriteCommand || instanceof DeleteCommand' and would reject it. Are we safe because validation rejects unexpected types?
assertions: The response identifies that the attack occurs during deserialization (when Jackson calls the setter methods on LoggingCommand), before the validation code runs
The response explains that even though validation will reject the object, the file-writing side effect may have already executed during the deserialization process

The response recommends using Jackson's PolymorphicTypeValidator or ObjectMapper configuration to whitelist allowed classes before deserialization, preventing dangerous classes from being instantiated

spreadsheet-processing.description: Excel/XLSX spreadsheet creation, editing, and analysis with openpyxl — formulas, formatting, data analysis, and recalculation

evals.name: Edge case: Formula structure creates circular reference
evals.prompt: Create a financial model where cell B10 calculates total revenue using =SUM(B2:B10), and B5 contains a formula that references the total in B10 to calculate a percentage.
assertions: The response identifies that =SUM(B2:B10) creates a circular reference because B10 is both the formula cell and part of its own range
The response corrects the formula to =SUM(B2:B9) or explains how to restructure the model to avoid the circular dependency

evals.name: Edge case: User wants to read calculated values but preserve formulas for later edits
evals.prompt: I need to read the calculated values from cells with formulas in an existing Excel file, then update some input cells and save the file. How should I load and save the workbook?
assertions: The response warns against using data_only=True for saving because it permanently replaces formulas with values

The response recommends loading normally without data_only=True, making edits, saving, then using recalc.py to update calculated values, OR loading with data_only=True only for reading and using a separate load operation for editing

evals.name: Edge case: User provides data and asks to create summary statistics in Excel
evals.prompt: I have sales data in columns A-D, rows 2-50. Create an Excel file with this data and add summary statistics at the bottom: total sales, average sales, and growth rate from first to last row.
assertions: The response uses Excel formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE, formula for growth) instead of calculating values in Python and hardcoding them
The response includes running recalc.py after saving to populate the formula values

java-framework-migration.description: Spring Boot and Java EE migration — namespace changes (javax to jakarta), dependency removal, version upgrades, and OpenRewrite automation

evals.name: Edge case: JAXB comes from a transitive dependency, not direct declaration
evals.prompt: After migrating to Spring Boot 3, I'm getting ClassNotFoundException for javax.xml.bind classes at runtime, but I don't see javax.xml.bind:jaxb-api in my pom.xml. What should I check?
assertions: The response suggests checking transitive dependencies using mvn dependency:tree to find which library is pulling in the old JAXB
The response recommends using dependency exclusions to block the transitive javax.xml.bind dependency and explicitly adding jakarta.xml.bind if XML binding is needed

evals.name: Edge case: Third-party library not yet compatible with Spring Boot 3
evals.prompt: I'm migrating to Spring Boot 3.2.0, but one of my dependencies (a custom library my team maintains) still uses javax.servlet imports and Spring Boot 2.x APIs. What should I do?
assertions: The response acknowledges the incompatibility and explains that the custom library must also be migrated to jakarta.servlet and Spring Boot 3 compatibility

The response suggests either updating the custom library first, or temporarily staying on Spring Boot 2.7.x until all dependencies are ready, rather than forcing the migration with incompatible dependencies

evals.name: Edge case: User jumps directly from Spring Boot 2.3 to 3.2 without intermediate steps
evals.prompt: I'm migrating a Spring Boot 2.3.x application directly to Spring Boot 3.2.0 and getting hundreds of compilation errors. Is this expected?
assertions: The response references the recommended migration order and explains that jumping directly from 2.3 to 3.2 skips important intermediate versions, particularly 2.7.x

The response recommends first upgrading to the latest Spring Boot 2.7.x, fixing any deprecation warnings, then proceeding to 3.2.x, as this provides a smoother migration path with better deprecation guidance

mathematical-optimization.description: Mixed-integer optimization with SCIP/PySCIPOpt — routing, assignment, scheduling with hard/soft constraints and subtour elimination

evals.name: Edge case: completely infeasible problem
evals.prompt: I need to assign 100 items to 5 bins, where each bin has a capacity of 2 units and each item requires at least 1 unit of space. Use SCIP to find an optimal assignment that minimizes cost.
assertions: Response acknowledges that the problem is mathematically infeasible (100 items cannot fit in 5 bins with capacity 2 each)
Response either detects infeasibility during model construction or reports that SCIP found no feasible solution with getNSols() == 0

evals.name: Edge case: time limit expires before finding any feasible solution
evals.prompt: Solve this extremely constrained routing problem with SCIP: 50 vehicles must visit 1000 locations each exactly once with very tight time windows, and set the time limit to 0.1 seconds. What should happen if no solution is found?
assertions: Response explains that if getNSols() returns 0 after optimization, the code should raise an error rather than trying to extract variable values
Response mentions checking model status and handling the no-solution case explicitly before calling getObjVal() or getVal()

evals.name: Edge case: user attempts to use Python abs() on solver expression
evals.prompt: I want to minimize the total absolute deviation from target values using SCIP. My code has: `model.setObjective(sum(abs(amount[i] - target[i]) for i in I), 'minimize')`. Will this work correctly?
assertions: Response identifies that Python's abs() cannot be used directly on solver expressions
Response provides the linearization pattern using slack variables with two inequality constraints per deviation term

vulnerability-scanning.description: Offline vulnerability scanning with Trivy — dependency analysis, CVE detection, air-gapped environments, and JSON report parsing

evals.name: Edge case: database directory exists but trivy.db file is missing
evals.prompt: I have a trivy-cache directory with a db/ subdirectory, but the trivy.db file inside was accidentally deleted. What happens when I run the offline scan script?
assertions: Response explains that the db_path check (os.path.exists) will fail and the script will exit before attempting to run Trivy
Response includes the error message prompting the user to download the database with the --download-db-only command

evals.name: Edge case: offline flags used but network access occurs anyway
evals.prompt: I'm running Trivy in an air-gapped environment with --offline-scan and --skip-db-update, but I'm still seeing network activity. What could be wrong?
assertions: Response investigates whether the --cache-dir flag is correctly pointing to the offline database location
Response mentions that if the database is not found at the specified cache directory, Trivy may attempt to download it despite offline flags

evals.name: Edge case: database file exists but is corrupted or incomplete
evals.prompt: The trivy.db file exists at the correct path and passes the os.path.exists check, but when I run the scan I get 'failed to initialize DB' errors. How should the script handle this?
assertions: Response acknowledges that the current skill only checks file existence, not database integrity
Response suggests either adding database validation steps or catching and reporting the 'failed to initialize DB' error with actionable guidance to re-download the database

document-template-processing.description: Word document (DOCX) template processing with python-docx — placeholder replacement, split placeholder handling, and formatting preservation

evals.name: Edge case: placeholder split across runs inside a nested table cell
evals.prompt: I have a Word template with a nested table (a table inside another table's cell). One of the cells has {{AMOUNT}} but it's split as {{AMO and UNT}} across two runs. Will the replace_all_placeholders function handle this?
assertions: Response operates at the paragraph level (using the concatenated paragraph text) rather than individual run level, so split placeholders will be detected and replaced correctly
Response confirms that nested tables are handled recursively to cover all levels of nesting

evals.name: Edge case: multi-section document with different headers per section
evals.prompt: My Word template has 3 sections, each with its own header containing different placeholders ({{SECTION1_TITLE}} in section 1, {{SECTION2_TITLE}} in section 2, etc.). Will the skill replace all of them?
assertions: Response processes headers and footers across all document sections, not just the body paragraphs
Response indicates that all placeholder replacements across all section headers will be performed

evals.name: Edge case: conditional marker itself is split across runs
evals.prompt: In my template, the text '{{IF_BONUS}}Your bonus is {{BONUS_AMOUNT}}{{END_IF_BONUS}}' has the marker {{IF_BO split across runs. How does the handle_conditional function deal with this?
assertions: Response explains that conditional markers are searched in the concatenated paragraph text, so split markers are still found
Response confirms that the paragraph-level rebuild approach handles split conditional markers correctly
